title: Introduction to Machine Learning
body: Machine learning is a field of artificial intelligence that gives computers the ability to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. Supervised learning trains models on labelled examples, while unsupervised learning discovers structure such as clusters in unlabelled data. Common algorithms include linear regression, decision trees, random forests and neural networks.

title: Deep Learning and Neural Networks Explained
body: Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers to learn hierarchical representations. Convolutional neural networks excel at image recognition, recurrent networks and transformers model sequences such as text and speech. Training deep networks requires large datasets, GPUs and techniques like dropout, batch normalization and backpropagation.

title: Natural Language Processing Fundamentals
body: Natural language processing (NLP) helps computers understand human language. A typical NLP pipeline performs tokenization, stop word removal, stemming or lemmatization, part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition. Modern NLP relies on transformer models such as BERT and GPT that produce contextual word embeddings.

title: How Search Engines Rank Results
body: Search engines build an inverted index that maps every term to the documents containing it. At query time the engine scores candidate documents with a relevance ranking function such as TF-IDF or BM25, which rewards rare terms and normalizes for document length. Signals like term proximity, title matches and freshness further improve ranking quality.

title: Building an Inverted Index
body: Document indexing starts by tokenizing text into terms. For each term the indexer stores a posting list with document identifiers, term frequencies and positions. Positions enable phrase queries and proximity scoring. Document frequency statistics are kept to compute inverse document frequency during relevance ranking.

title: Keyword Extraction with RAKE and TF-IDF
body: Keyword extraction identifies the most important words and phrases in a document. RAKE splits text on stop words and punctuation to find candidate phrases and scores them using word degree and frequency. TF-IDF weights terms that are frequent in a document but rare across the corpus. Extracted keywords power tagging, summarization and search suggestions.

title: Getting Started with React
body: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from reusable components. Components manage state with hooks such as useState and useEffect and re-render efficiently through the virtual DOM. React apps are often created with Vite and communicate with a backend through REST APIs using fetch.

title: React Hooks Deep Dive
body: Hooks let function components use state and lifecycle features. useEffect runs side effects like data fetching; always return a cleanup function to cancel requests with an AbortController. useMemo and useCallback memoize expensive values, and custom hooks such as useDebounce encapsulate reusable logic for search-as-you-type inputs.

title: Node.js Event Loop and Asynchronous Programming
body: Node.js runs JavaScript on the server with a single-threaded event loop. Asynchronous programming with callbacks, promises and async/await keeps the server responsive while waiting for I/O such as database queries or HTTP requests. Express is a popular framework for building REST APIs in Node.js.

title: Designing RESTful APIs
body: A REST API exposes resources through URLs and standard HTTP methods: GET reads, POST creates, PUT and PATCH update, and DELETE removes. Good API design uses consistent naming, pagination, meaningful status codes, validation errors and versioning. OpenAPI documents describe endpoints for clients and tooling.

title: Python FastAPI Tutorial
body: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building APIs with type hints. It validates requests with Pydantic, generates OpenAPI documentation automatically and supports asynchronous endpoints with async and await. Run the application with Uvicorn and use dependency injection to share database connections.

title: MongoDB Basics for Developers
body: MongoDB is a document database that stores JSON-like BSON documents in collections. Queries filter documents with operators such as $in and $regex, indexes speed up lookups, and the aggregation pipeline transforms data. The Motor driver provides an asynchronous Python client suitable for FastAPI applications.

title: Database Indexing Strategies
body: Database indexes trade extra storage and slower writes for fast reads. B-tree indexes support range queries and sorting, compound indexes cover queries on several fields, and text indexes enable basic full-text search. Analyze slow queries with explain plans before adding new indexes.

title: Docker for Beginners
body: Docker packages applications and their dependencies into containers that run the same everywhere. A Dockerfile describes how to build an image, and docker compose starts multi-container applications such as a web frontend, an API server and a MongoDB database with a single command.

title: Kubernetes Deployment Guide
body: Kubernetes orchestrates containers across a cluster. Deployments manage replicated pods, services provide stable networking and ingress exposes HTTP routes. Horizontal pod autoscaling adjusts replicas based on CPU usage, and rolling updates deploy new versions without downtime.

title: Improving Web Application Performance
body: Fast web applications load quickly and respond instantly. Techniques include caching API responses, compressing assets, lazy loading images, debouncing user input and code splitting JavaScript bundles. Measure performance with Lighthouse and real user monitoring before optimizing.

title: Spelling Correction in Search
body: Users often misspell queries. Spelling correction compares each query word with the index vocabulary using edit distance such as Damerau-Levenshtein and proposes the closest frequent word. A did you mean suggestion helps users recover from typos without retyping the whole query.

title: Query Understanding and Intent Detection
body: Query understanding interprets what a user wants. Intent detection classifies queries as informational, navigational, transactional or question style. Query expansion adds synonyms so that a search for car also finds automobile, while exclusion operators and quoted phrases let users refine results precisely.

title: Electric Cars and the Future of Transport
body: Electric vehicles replace combustion engines with batteries and electric motors. Falling battery prices and expanding charging networks make the electric automobile practical for daily driving. Renewable energy on the grid further reduces lifetime emissions compared with petrol cars.

title: Renewable Energy Sources
body: Solar panels, wind turbines and hydroelectric dams generate electricity without burning fossil fuels. Energy storage with large batteries smooths the variable output of solar and wind power. Renewable energy is now the cheapest source of new electricity in many countries.

title: Climate Change Explained
body: Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns driven mainly by greenhouse gas emissions from burning coal, oil and gas. Consequences include rising sea levels, heatwaves and extreme weather. Cutting emissions and adapting infrastructure are the main responses.

title: A Beginner's Guide to Healthy Cooking
body: Healthy cooking starts with fresh vegetables, whole grains and lean protein. Steaming and roasting preserve nutrients better than deep frying. Plan meals for the week, cook in batches and season with herbs and spices instead of extra salt.

title: The History of the Film Industry
body: The film industry began with silent movies in the 1890s. Sound arrived in the late 1920s, colour spread in the 1950s and digital cameras and streaming services transformed how movies are produced and watched in the twenty-first century.

title: Transformers: Attention Is All You Need
body: The transformer architecture replaced recurrence with self-attention, letting models process all tokens of a sequence in parallel. Multi-head attention captures different relationships between words. Transformers power large language models used for translation, summarization, question answering and semantic search.

title: Semantic Search with Embeddings
body: Semantic search retrieves documents by meaning rather than exact keywords. Text is converted into dense vector embeddings and similar vectors are found with approximate nearest neighbour indexes. Hybrid search combines BM25 keyword relevance with embedding similarity for the best results.
